validity_note: Read down in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (26 Sep 2018): an authentication record does not include the metadata that Regulation 26(c) of the Aadhaar (Authentication) Regulations, 2016 provided for, and that regulation was struck down. The whole of section 2 carries the banner because the corpus item is the section; the disposition is about clause (d) alone.
judgment_quote: Section 2(d) which pertains to authentication records, such records would not include metadata as mentioned in Regulation 26(c) of the Aadhaar (Authentication) Regulations, 2016. Therefore, this provision … in the present form is struck down.

validity_note: Read down in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (26 Sep 2018): 'benefit' takes its meaning ejusdem generis from 'subsidies', so section 7 reaches only expenditure charged to the Consolidated Fund and not a benefit an individual has earned. The text as enacted is wider than what it now means.
judgment_quote: the expression ‘benefit’ has to be read ejusdem generis with the preceding word ‘subsidies’. … We also make it clear that a benefit which is earned by an individual (e.g. pension by a government employee) cannot be covered under Section 7 of the Act

instrument: Prevention of Money-Laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005
provision: Rule 9(a)(17), as amended by the Seventh Amendment Rules, 2017
validity_note: Struck down in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (26 Sep 2018). Mandatory linking of a bank account to an Aadhaar number failed proportionality. This instrument is not in this corpus; the row exists so that a claim about Aadhaar-and-banking cannot be made here without meeting it.
judgment_quote: Thus the amendment to Rule 9, by the Seventh Amendment Rules, 2017, in the present form, is held to be unconstitutional.

instrument: Department of Telecommunications circular dated 23 March 2017
validity_note: Struck down in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (26 Sep 2018). Re-verification of every existing mobile subscriber through Aadhaar e-KYC was disproportionate and unreasonable state compulsion. Not in this corpus; the row exists so the claim cannot be made here without meeting it.
judgment_quote: The Circular dated March 23, 2017 is declared as unconstitutional

validity_note: Sub-section (1) was read down in 2018 to require an opportunity of hearing, and the Aadhaar and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019 (Act 14 of 2019), s. 14 put that requirement into the statute, so the read-down is spent. Sub-section (2) as it then stood was struck down and s. 14 re-enacted it in amended form — 'Secretary' for 'Joint Secretary', with an Oversight Committee — and the current text has not been tested.
judgment_quote: Section 33(1) of the Aadhaar Act is read down by clarifying that an individual, whose information is sought to be released, shall be afforded an opportunity of hearing.

validity_note: The 2018 judgment held section 47 constitutional and recommended that it be amended to let a victim complain; Act 14 of 2019, s. 20 inserted the proviso that does exactly that. So this is a recommendation Parliament took, not a disposition that binds the current text.
judgment_quote: It would be in the fitness of things if Section 47 is amended by allowing individual/victim whose right is violated, to file a complaint and initiate the proceedings.
That portion of Section 57 of the Aadhaar Act which enables body corporate and individual to seek authentication is held to be unconstitutional.
Metabase relating to transaction, as provided in Regulation 26 of the aforesaid Regulations in the present form, is held to be impermissible, which needs suitable amendment.
